title: S6 report
question: Does D3's DDL apply on PostgreSQL 18 with pgvector and pg_textsearch; do the v1 trace rows and typed queries work; does the revised statement key settle the meaning key?
method: Report rendered from the evidence catalog over the S6 records, with the corrected DDL as a diff against D3's blocks (code/s6g_diff.py) and design implications tied to D3 sections and OPEN items. The spike ran on the project-local interim cluster; cs_spike_s6 and cs_s6_app were dropped at the end (step 11).

agents.separation: coordinator brief; wrote only code/s6*, results/s6/, records/s6.*, S6-report*

outputs.role: corrected DDL as a diff against D3

results.name: ddl_fixes
results.note: F1 regconfig cast (error), F2 kind CHECK (gap)

results.name: design_implications
results.note: rows in the report's design-implications table

conclusion: D3 becomes migration 0001 with two DDL fixes, a BM25 kind list without math_display (with caption), corrected family_profile and evidence queries, one naming convention between the compiled schema rows and the knowledge rows, a schema_slot key for value-class attributes, ParseStatus aligned with the parse_status CHECKs and an ops.task (run_id, unit_key) index; the queue design holds, a two-branch claim is the scaling option; the revised statement key brings claim keys within three pairs of meaning keys and no restated facts were found, so migration 0001 needs no meaning-key column. Evidence for ADR-0016 (PostgreSQL as the single authority): every store mechanism tested works in the one database.
